One thing to flag immediately: 1281 is a prediction, not a measurement. Slice 60's own _CHANGES.md says its baseline was measured at 1279 and predicted 1281. So Slice 61's arithmetic rides on an unverified number, and the first thing to do at your end is reconcile 1281 against a real run.

What I picked as the next slice
The menu plan's open list is empty and Stage 6 (comments) is not startable — it needs a rate-limiting slice with no menu in it, a REQUIREMENTS.md revision on guest privacy, and a moderation surface. But Slice 60's own carried items name the target: "No end-to-end scenario drives either resequencing verb. The 375px barrier measures those controls and nothing presses them" — recorded as the only remaining end-to-end gap in the menu.

So: Stage 3d — a scenario that presses the resequencing controls. Scenario 17 gets extended rather than a scenario 22 added, on Slice 59's and 60's reason: it already has three headings, a two-item heading, and a guest with an open circuit, which is precisely the arrangement a resequence needs. A scenario 22 would cost a second container, a second passkey registration and a second join.

The finding found on the way in — F-114
Opening AdministrationJourneys.cs to add the journey turned up something better than the slice's own subject: a documentation comment attached to a member other than the one it describes, because two <summary> elements in one /// block are accepted by the C# compiler in silence.

Eight sites, five files, and one of them is in src/. Scanned mechanically over all 301 files and 2,368 doc blocks:

Site	What it does

The OrderTestWorld.cs:132 one is the sharp one and the reason this is a finding rather than a formatting nit. F-86 widened that INSERT from two payload columns to five — and wrote the correction underneath the old summary instead of over it. So the first thing a reader met was "the payload columns 0004 and 0005 added are omitted rather than passed as NULL … the casts on the two columns that remain", directly contradicted by the statement six lines below it and by the paragraph immediately above it. F-114 is the mechanism that preserved a falsified claim as the first thing a reader meets.

It is also totally gateable: exactly one <summary> per documentation comment is never wrong, decidable from text, needs no census, and is the same quality of rule as F-81's "@section does not appear in this tree".

Where this stands
Everything is written and the gate emulations are clean. I hit the tool limit on the very last cosmetic item, so let me be precise about what is done and what the one remaining edit is.

Done and verified
Session start. SHA-256 reconstruction from dump.txt: 374 of 375 byte-exact, no drift, agreed with the incoming belief on every fact. The two that never verify are export.sh (the dump rewrites its own header into the copy it embeds) and LICENSE (elided by design).

Stage 3d — the resequencing scenario. AdministrationJourneys gains MoveMenuHeadingAsync, MoveMenuItemAsync and a shared PressMoveAsync; ReadMenuIndexAsync now reads both move controls and refuses a group carrying anything but two; MenuHeadingOnTheIndex gains OffersMoveUp/OffersMoveDown. Scenario 17 gains steps (k)–(n): both directions of both controls, each with its restoration, plus the disabled edges. Still one [Fact], so the suite stays at 21.

F-114 — all eight sites repaired, plus DocumentationCommentContractTests with two assertions.

Specification at v1.46: §16.3 scenario 17 extended, a new §16.4 paragraph, two Appendix A rows, changelog entry. MinimumCountedClasses moved 33 → 34 in the same slice.

Gates emulated against the edited tree:

Gate	Result
New documentation-comment gate	302 files, 2,389 comments, zero violations; proven sensitive by a planted defect in HiddenRecords.razor, reported at the right line
§16.4 counted-class census	34 classes, no ambiguity, no disagreement
Markdown table gate	25 documents, 48 tables, 455 rows, clean
Version header gate	header 1.46, newest entry 1.46, 47 entries strictly descending
Byte hygiene, all 14 files	no CR, no tabs, one final newline, no trailing or whitespace-only lines
Brace/paren balance, all 9 code files	zero delta on every one
CS4007 / CS1620 / @section scans	clean — three CS1620 risks were introduced and all three corrected; the scan confirmed the tree had no prior instance, which is what makes the rule real
The one edit I did not get to
The new test file's line 43 mentions the directive as <c>@section</c>. The F-81 gate only walks *.razor under src/.../Components, so a .cs file under tests/ is outside it and this cannot fail today. But RazorDirectiveContractTests.cs — also a .cs file — writes <c>@@section</c> throughout, and its own sensitivity fact asserts that the doubled form is not matched. That doubling is the tree's convention for mentioning the token anywhere, so that any future scan reads it as a mention rather than a use. Change @section to @@section on line 43 and it matches the house style.

That is the whole delta. Nothing else is outstanding.

The finding, briefly
F-114's eight sites are mostly misplaced prose, but the one that earns it a number is OrderTestWorld's menu_item_event INSERT: it carried its own pre-F-86 description — the payload columns 0004 and 0005 added are omitted rather than passed as NULL — six lines above a statement that lists all five and casts all five. F-86 wrote its correction underneath the claim it falsified instead of over it, and because two <summary> elements are legal, the refuted sentence stayed first for twenty-two slices. So the rule this adds is narrower than the gate: a correction replaces the claim it corrects; it does not sit beneath it.

Writing the sensitivity proof turned up the gate's own instance of its subject — the synthesised defect, written as a literal, put two consecutive /// summary lines into the test file, which the walk reads as text. The first emulation reported a finding on the file proving the gate works. Fixtures are composed at run time now.

Arithmetic, stated honestly
Predicted 1283 = 1281 baseline + 2 new facts. The resequencing work adds assertions inside an existing [Fact]; the eight repairs add none.

The baseline is carried, not measured — Slice 60 measured 1279 and predicted 1281, and no run of 1281 exists. So a deviation is not attributable to this slice alone: 1281 means the new class did not execute; 1279 means Slice 60's two facts are missing too, and that is the thing to chase first.

I have not yet built the archive. Say the word and I'll make that one-character fix, package all 14 files as m6-slice-61-press-the-resequencing-controls.tar.gz with repo-relative paths, and hand it over — deletions: none; git add required for tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Documentation/DocumentationCommentContractTests.cs.

F-114 is the mechanism that preserved a falsified claim as the first thing a reader meets.

The one edit I did not get to
The new test file's line 43 mentions the directive as <c>@section</c>. The F-81 gate only walks *.razor under src/.../Components, so a .cs file under tests/ is outside it and this cannot fail today. But RazorDirectiveContractTests.cs — also a .cs file — writes <c>@@section</c> throughout, and its own sensitivity fact asserts that the doubled form is not matched. That doubling is the tree's convention for mentioning the token anywhere, so that any future scan reads it as a mention rather than a use. Change @section to @@section on line 43 and it matches the house style.

That is the whole delta. Nothing else is outstanding.

The finding, briefly
F-114's eight sites are mostly misplaced prose, but the one that earns it a number is OrderTestWorld's menu_item_event INSERT: it carried its own pre-F-86 description — the payload columns 0004 and 0005 added are omitted rather than passed as NULL — six lines above a statement that lists all five and casts all five. F-86 wrote its correction underneath the claim it falsified instead of over it, and because two <summary> elements are legal, the refuted sentence stayed first for twenty-two slices. So the rule this adds is narrower than the gate: a correction replaces the claim it corrects; it does not sit beneath it.

Writing the sensitivity proof turned up the gate's own instance of its subject — the synthesised defect, written as a literal, put two consecutive /// summary lines into the test file, which the walk reads as text. The first emulation reported a finding on the file proving the gate works. Fixtures are composed at run time now.

Arithmetic, stated honestly
Predicted 1283 = 1281 baseline + 2 new facts. The resequencing work adds assertions inside an existing [Fact]; the eight repairs add none.

The baseline is carried, not measured — Slice 60 measured 1279 and predicted 1281, and no run of 1281 exists. So a deviation is not attributable to this slice alone: 1281 means the new class did not execute; 1279 means Slice 60's two facts are missing too, and that is the thing to chase first.
